core_obligations: Handle n = 0 as the author does, then assume n > 0 and reduce a very ample invertible sheaf to the model case X = P^r_k, L = O_X(1) (proof lines 4244-4247).

Identify V = H^0(X, L) = kT_0 + ... + kT_r with the linear forms and show that the sections vanishing at the k-rational point x form a codimension one subspace W that generates the homogeneous prime ideal of x (proof lines 4248-4253).

For each i, use x_i != x to get a homogeneous prime p_i with W not contained in p_i, and conclude over the infinite field k that W is not the union of the W cap p_i, which produces the required section (proof lines 4253-4256).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to P^r_k with O_X(1) by the definition of very ampleness (proof lines 4244-4247).
Describe the vanishing locus at x as the codimension one subspace W of the space of linear forms (proof lines 4248-4253).
Use infinitude of k to escape the finitely many hyperplanes W cap p_i (proof lines 4253-4256).
difficulty_reason: The statement produces a global section of a very ample invertible sheaf on a finite type k-scheme that vanishes at a prescribed k-rational point x and at none of finitely many other points x_1,...,x_n (statement lines 4232-4241). The proof first reduces a very ample L on X to the model case X = P^r_k with L = O_X(1) (proof lines 4244-4247), then identifies V = H^0(X, O_X(1)) with the linear forms and the sections vanishing at x with a codimension one subspace W that generates the homogeneous prime ideal of x (proof lines 4248-4253); the non-formal step is the final one, where each x_i != x gives a homogeneous prime p_i not containing W, so W is not the union of the finitely many W cap p_i because k is infinite (proof lines 4253-4256). The claim is H2: the reduction is standard and the last step is the finite-union-of-proper-subspaces argument over an infinite field.
